scope: Complete 14-run terminal comparison: ReAct GPT/Opus/Kimi and AI Scientist Docker runs, plus shared native Codex/Claude Code/OpenHands results.
native_reports: Byte-identical to v4_original; IDs and trace IDs are reused, not new executions.
resource_settings: Docker trials used 2 CPU equivalents, 4 GiB RAM, 256 PIDs. Native agents had no configured per-trial CPU/RAM cap.
deadlines: No whole-trial deadline for ReAct/AI Scientist. Native timeout replacements are described in v4_original/provenance.json.
terminal_timeout: Mixed historical settings: original Corral tool allowed up to 3600s; later ReAct resumes enforced 600s, retaining the 120s default. AI Scientist retained its original image/tool maximum.
recovery: Artifact-blocked ReAct trials were resumed with checkpoint ownership normalization; completed non-target outcomes retained. Some trials still ended with OOM/provider/budget errors, which remain represented.
langfuse: IDs are deterministic from benchmark_run_id and execution_id. Local receipts do not independently verify remote availability. Shared trace IDs can contain superseded observations; use report evaluation hash and local checkpoint to identify final content.
